description: Input that does not conform to the did-url rule ends processing with INVALID_DID_URL
Method names must be lowercase, so this does not conform to the did-url rule
A failed resolution surfaces as a resolution error. Requires the did:test resolver to return a NOT_FOUND result for any DID other than did:test:deref
No service, path or strategy-defining query parameter, so the DID document is returned
A fragment does not change the strategy; it is applied to the returned DID document when the handler result is used
versionId only affects resolution, not the handling strategy (Query Parameters Step)
service=%23files resolves to did:test:deref#files and matches the relative id #files
open: Section 5.3 only describes a DID URL that has a path; with no path, the serviceEndpoint is assumed to be used as is

description: An absolute DID URL in the service parameter matches the relative id #files
service=%23mirror matches the absolute id did:test:deref#mirror. One of its two endpoints returns 404, so the client must try the other one (whichever it picks first) and return mirror.json
The selected service's type DIDCommMessaging defines its own handling strategy, so the Default Service Handler is not used. A client with no DIDCommMessaging handler raises HANDLER_NOT_FOUND
The Default Service Handler does not process relativeRef, so the resource URL is the service endpoint unchanged
open: Section 3 Example 2 and Section 12.7.1 describe relativeRef being combined with the service endpoint, which contradicts the note in Section 5.3

description: service=files with no leading #
open: Strict RFC3986 reference resolution turns files into did:files, which matches nothing; Section 3 Example 2 and DID Core 1.0 practice match it to #files

description: No service matches, so SERVICE_NOT_FOUND is raised and processing continues to the Default DID Document Step
open: Section 5.2 says to stop further processing instead of continuing

description: More than one service parameter raises MULTIPLE_SERVICE_PARAMETERS and continues to the Default DID Document Step
The service path /files/ is stripped and the rest is appended to the endpoint path. The path also matches the #root PathHandler, so this checks the Services Step runs first
Dot segments that stay inside the endpoint path are removed and allowed
The normalized resource path escapes the endpoint path .../resources/files/. Returning the canary secret.json means the client fetched it
open: Section 12.7.1 suggests INVALID_DID_URL for the same case

description: Percent-encoded dot segments are decoded before normalization, so this also escapes .../resources/files/. Returning the canary secret.json means the client fetched it
open: Section 12.7.1 is non-normative; Section 5.3 does not say whether to decode before removing dot segments

description: The DID URL path does not start with the service path /files/
open: Section 5.3 does not define what happens when the DID URL path does not start with the service path

description: /image.png matches /, /image and /image.png; the longest match #SecuredImage is selected and its secondary type LinkedResource defines the strategy
#image is the longest match; PathService defines no strategy, so the Default Service Handler is used
open: Stripping /image leaves /x, and appending that to /image/ gives a double slash. The PathHandlers Step also says to raise PATH_HANDLER_HANDLER_NOT_DEFINED when the secondary type defines no strategy

description: /image is a string prefix of /imagex.json but not a whole path segment
open: Section 5.4 says the entire path value must be present at the start of the DID URL path, without saying whether matching is by character or by segment

description: Only #root (path /) matches
#bare has PathHandler as its only type, which Section 5.3 sends to the Default Service Handler
open: The PathHandlers Step would raise PATH_HANDLER_HANDLER_NOT_DEFINED instead; also has the double-slash question

description: #dupA and #dupB both match with the same length, so MULTIPLE_MATCHING_PATH_HANDLERS is raised and processing continues to the Default DID Document Step
open: Section 5.4 says to stop processing and return the error; the PathHandlers Step says to continue
